## Purpose and Scope

This RAD provides illustrative patterns and logical design guidance for realizing the foundational Cloud and Infrastructure Security controls across the enterprise AWS environment. It covers the cross-cutting security services that span all workload types:

**Governing ABBs**:
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CSPM-2.6.03 — Cloud Security Posture Management](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CSPM-2.6.03.md)
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-SECRETS-MGMT-2.6.05 — Secrets Management](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-SECRETS-MGMT-2.6.05.md)
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-DATA-PROT-2.6.07 — Cloud Data Protection](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-DATA-PROT-2.6.07.md)
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-NETWORK-SEC-2.6.08 — Cloud Network Security Governance](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-NETWORK-SEC-2.6.08.md)

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-RAD-3.6.01.md#aws-organizations-structure]

### AWS Organizations Structure

The Cloud Security Foundations architecture assumes a multi-account AWS Organizations structure with dedicated accounts for security tooling. The following account structure is the reference model:

```
AWS Organizations Root
├── Security OU
│   ├── Security Tooling Account     ← Security Hub delegated admin, GuardDuty admin, Inspector admin
│   └── Log Archive Account          ← CloudTrail logs, VPC flow logs, Config history (immutable)
├── Infrastructure OU
│   ├── Network Account              ← Transit Gateway, centralized egress, shared VPC
│   └── Shared Services Account      ← SSM, Secrets Manager cross-account, AMI pipeline
├── Workload OU
│   ├── PHI Production OU            ← SCP: PHI-restricted controls applied
│   │   ├── PHI Prod Account 1
│   │   └── PHI Prod Account N
│   ├── Production OU
│   │   └── Non-PHI Prod Accounts
│   └── Non-Production OU
│       └── Dev/Staging/Test Accounts
└── Management Account               ← AWS Organizations management only; no workloads
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-RAD-3.6.01.md#security-hub-organization-deployment]

### Security Hub Organization Deployment

```
Security Tooling Account (Delegated Administrator)
├── Security Hub — Organization Admin
│   ├── AFSBP Standard (AWS Foundational Security Best Practices) — enabled all accounts
│   ├── CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1.4 — enabled all accounts
│   └── NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 — enabled PHI OU accounts
├── GuardDuty — Organization Admin
│   ├── Auto-enable: ALL (new + existing accounts)
│   └── Protection Plans: S3, EKS Audit, Lambda Network, Malware Protection, RDS
├── AWS Inspector — Organization Admin
│   ├── EC2 scanning (SSM agent required)
│   ├── ECR enhanced scanning (on-push)
│   └── Lambda function scanning
└── IAM Access Analyzer — Organization Admin
    └── Unused access analysis enabled
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-RAD-3.6.01.md#key-design-principles]

### Key Design Principles

CMKs are scoped per environment and per data classification tier to limit the blast radius of key compromise and to maintain clear audit trails:

| Key Purpose | Key Alias | Usage | Rotation |
|---|---|---|---|
| PHI data — production | `alias/phi-prod-{service}` | RDS encryption, S3 SSE-KMS for PHI buckets | Annual (auto) |
| Non-PHI production | `alias/prod-{service}` | Production non-PHI storage | Annual (auto) |
| Secrets encryption | `alias/secrets-manager` | Secrets Manager secret encryption | Annual (auto) |
| Log archive | `alias/log-archive` | CloudTrail and flow log S3 bucket encryption | Annual (auto) |
| Non-production | `alias/nonprod` | Dev/staging environments | Annual (auto) |

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-RAD-3.6.01.md#key-policy-pattern]

### Key Policy Pattern

Every CMK key policy follows the principle of separated administration and usage:

```json
{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "KeyAdministration",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::{account}:role/key-administrators"},
      "Action": ["kms:Create*", "kms:Describe*", "kms:Enable*", "kms:List*",
                 "kms:Put*", "kms:Update*", "kms:Revoke*", "kms:Disable*",
                 "kms:Get*", "kms:Delete*", "kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion", "kms:CancelKeyDeletion"],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "KeyUsage",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::{account}:role/{workload-role}"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-RAD-3.6.01.md#database-credential-pattern-rdsaurora]

### Database Credential Pattern (RDS/Aurora)

```
Workload (ECS Task / Lambda)
  └─→ Secrets Manager (via VPC endpoint)
        ├── Secret: /prod/claims-db/db-credentials
        │   ├── Rotation: AWS-managed (SecretsManagerRDSPostgreSQLRotationSingleUser)
        │   ├── Rotation interval: 30 days (PHI) / 90 days (non-PHI)
        │   └── Key: alias/phi-prod-claims-db CMK
        └── KMS endpoint: via VPC interface endpoint
```
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-RAD-3.6.01.md#cross-account-secret-access-pattern]

### Cross-Account Secret Access Pattern

For shared services (e.g., shared Secrets Manager in the Shared Services account):

- Resource-based policy on the secret grants `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` to the specific workload role ARN in the consuming account
- The consuming workload assumes its task role; the task role has an identity policy permitting `sts:AssumeRole` to the cross-account access role
- No wildcard principals in cross-account secret policies

- `iac/formations/security/aws-config/` — Config rules, conformance packs, remediation actions
- `iac/formations/security/kms/` — CMK creation patterns and key policy templates
- `iac/formations/security/secrets-manager/` — Secrets Manager resource patterns and rotation configuration
